raylibr handoff

Source: handoff.md

Last updated: 2026-10-31. State of main: d8997134 (in sync with GitHub). Latest release: v6.0.4 (tag on 33d27785, GitHub release published), prepared as raylibr’s first CRAN submission. Not yet submitted.

Read CLAUDE.md first: it covers code generation, hand-maintained files, building, testing, the website and demo assets.

1. Open tasks

1.1 Finish the CRAN submission (in progress)

  1. win-builder results. The 6.0.4 tarball was uploaded to win-builder for R-devel and R-release on 2026-10-30. The results are emailed to the maintainer (jeroen@jeroenjanssens.com), not visible anywhere else. The first email has arrived; its contents have not been reviewed yet.
    • For each email: note R-devel vs R-release, the Status: line, and the full text of every NOTE/WARNING/ERROR. Expect one NOTE: “CRAN incoming feasibility … New submission”. Check it for “Possibly misspelled words” or URL problems.
    • The links in the email point to the full check and install logs, which win-builder deletes after a few days.
  2. cran-comments.md: replace the line starting with TODO before submitting: with the win-builder results. If they show a new NOTE, explain it there (or fix it).
  3. Fix anything win-builder finds. If code changes are needed, release 6.0.5 the same way as 6.0.4 (section 3.3), since v6.0.4 is already tagged and published. Don’t move published tags.
  4. Submit: the maintainer runs devtools::submit_cran() from a checkout of main and clicks the confirmation email. This step is theirs.
  5. After CRAN’s response: answer reviewer comments, or tag the CRAN release state if CRAN asks for changes.

1.2 Known issues (not started)

  • Audio functions without an audio device (untested, may crash). Sound, music and audio-stream functions likely crash R when init_audio_device() hasn’t been called, the same way drawing functions crashed without a window. A guard like the window guard (section 2.1) would fix it. Not investigated; needs testing with real sound objects.
  • Name overlaps (decision: keep).
    • raylibr’s key enum hides data.table’s key() if data.table is attached before raylibr; attached after, key$space breaks. key(dt) keeps working either way.
    • file_exists(), file_copy(), file_move() and file_rename() overlap with fs/xfun. Maintainer decided to keep exporting all 27 file helpers.
    • The color class clash with colorspace is fixed (section 2.4), so no renaming is needed.
  • 452 help pages still have @examplesIf FALSE. They’re functions that need a window, audio, files or GPU objects. Possible improvement: handwrite examples that wrap them in raylibr_screenshot().
  • -Wextra warnings in raygui (missing field initializers). R and CRAN don’t use -Wextra, so they are left as upstream wrote them.
  • “Array buffer allocation failed” appeared in headless Chrome for the Hello World webR demo, which ran at about 337 FPS there. Most likely a headless artifact; the demo kept rendering. Recheck if users report it in a normal browser.
  • A local warning about R’s own header: on this Mac, every install warns about R_ext/Boolean.h ... -Wfixed-enum-extension. It comes from R’s header vs. Apple clang 21, not raylibr, and doesn’t occur on CI or CRAN.

2. What changed in this session (2026-10-28 to 10-31)

31 commits since v6.0.2, released as 6.0.3 and 6.0.4. Details are in NEWS.md; the important design decisions:

2.1 Window guard

Functions that need an OpenGL context or a GLFW window used to crash R (segfault or GLFW assertion) without a window. Now they stop with “draw_circle() needs an open window. Call init_window() first.” - needs_window() in data-raw/generate.R holds the name rules. The generated wrappers call raylibr_require_window() (in src/raylibr.h). 21 hand-written wrappers in src/manual_wrappers.cpp call it too. - The rules were checked by calling every wrapped function without a window in a fresh R process: all 204 that crashed are covered. Exempt pure rlgl getters: rlGetVersion, rlGetPixelFormatName, rlGetCullDistanceNear/Far. - Cost: one flag read (about 1 ns; a draw call from R is about 16 µs).

2.2 CRAN preparation

  • Tests: skip_if_no_gl() (tests/testthat/helper-gl.R). Window tests run with RAYLIBR_GL=true (CI), skip on CRAN, CI and Linux without a display, and otherwise run (testthat::test_local() on a desktop).
  • Examples: has_display() (R/extra.R) is TRUE only with RAYLIBR_GL=true, or in an interactive session with a display. So R CMD check never opens windows unless asked to.
  • Examples that run anywhere: runs_without_window() in the generator. 369 run unconditionally. They were checked CRAN-style and with an integer-division sanitizer build.
  • Demo assets moved from inst/demo_resources/ to assets/, which is excluded from the package. raylibr_resource() downloads them on first use into tools::R_user_dir("raylibr", "cache"). It tries the v<version> tag first, then main (development versions with four version components use main). With RAYLIBR_ASSETS set it reads that folder instead. inst/assets.txt lists every asset (a test checks this), and a folder name downloads the whole folder. The webR build bundles assets/. Tarball went from 6.8 MB to 2.7 MB.
  • Bundled Raylib: data-raw/make_raylib_tarball.R rebuilds inst/raylib-6.0-minimal.tar.gz from the official 6.0 release, minus unused backends (RGFW, SDL, DRM, Android, Win32, memory) and the software renderer. The original bundled src/ was identical to the release.
  • Credits: 17 copyright holders in Authors@R (role cph), and every file in src/external is listed in inst/COPYRIGHTS.
  • Logging: src/log.cpp routes Raylib’s log through REprintf() (set up in .onLoad()), at warning level by default. Messages from other threads (the audio thread) are dropped on desktop. webR compiles without the thread check.
  • Compiler settings: Raylib’s Makefile now gets R’s CC, AR, CFLAGS and CPICFLAGS (RAYLIB_MAKE_ARGS in src/Makevars.in and .win). “GNU make” is in SystemRequirements.
  • Linux headers: configure checks for the X11 extension and OpenGL headers and stops with a list of missing headers and package names. SystemRequirements lists them.
  • raygui patches (inst/raygui.h, all marked raylibr:): the fread()/fgets() results are checked; GuiFontIconBaking() is only compiled with RAYGUI_FONT_ICONS_BAKING; a negative glyph count is treated as zero, also in the allocation sizes. The diagnostic pragma in src/raygui_impl.cpp is gone.
  • Raylib patches (tools/patch_raylib.R, applied at install and in the webR build): HiDPI scale in BeginMode2D(), and CloseWindow() resets window flags.

2.3 Other fixes

  • transform() was renamed to raylib_transform() (class "raylib_transform"). It hid base::transform() and broke ggplot2 scales. Only Transform was renamed: the maintainer rejected renaming all classes.
  • gen_image_checked() requires positive check sizes. Zero crashed R with SIGFPE on x86 (ARM returns 0, so macOS didn’t show it).
  • gui_scroll_panel() returns a real rectangle for view.
  • is_color() returns TRUE/FALSE for every input.
  • raygui resets its font in init_window(). It kept the first window’s freed font, so text vanished, sizes were garbage, and R could crash.
  • load_shader*("") passes NULL to Raylib.

2.4 S3 methods leave other packages’ objects alone

Generated struct methods ($, [[, print, as.character, …) call NextMethod() unless the object is an external pointer. This fixed colorspace’s S4 color objects without renaming the class.

3. How to work on this repo

3.1 Conventions

  • Commits: author is Jeroen Janssens. Never add Co-Authored-By or any AI attribution.
  • Python: use uv, never pip.
  • Commit on main (the maintainer’s workflow) and push after local checks pass. Ask before outward-facing actions: tags, releases, CRAN, emails.
  • roxygen2 must be 7.3.3 (matches RoxygenNote). The local default is 8.x, which rewrites every Rd file. Install 7.3.3 into a temp library: remotes::install_version("roxygen2", "7.3.3", lib = "/tmp/rox733"), then run with R_LIBS=/tmp/rox733 Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise()'. If a run shows \link[=...] changes or Config/roxygen2/version in DESCRIPTION, version 8 ran: revert man/, NAMESPACE and DESCRIPTION.
  • Regenerating code: Rscript data-raw/generate.R, then Rcpp::compileAttributes(), then roxygen 7.3.3. Afterwards there should be no other changes, because the Codegen check workflow verifies this.
  • Stale builds: “library ‘raylib’ not found” means src/raylib_built is stale. Delete it (and src/*.o) and reinstall. If an interrupted install left 00LOCK-raylibr in the library folder, remove it.

3.2 Testing

  • RAYLIBR_GL=true Rscript -e 'testthat::test_local()' runs all tests (about 1113).
  • CRAN-like test run: unset NOT_CRAN, CI and RAYLIBR_GL, then testthat::test_dir("tests/testthat", package = "raylibr", load_package = "installed"). Window and audio tests must skip.
  • Local CRAN check: build from a clean export (git archive HEAD), then env -u RAYLIBR_GL -u RAYLIBR_ASSETS -u CI -u NOT_CRAN R_USER_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/x/cache R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual <tarball>.
  • Site build: RAYLIBR_GL=true RAYLIBR_ASSETS=$PWD/assets. Build articles one at a time with pkgdown::build_article(); a batch build hung once, before the raygui font fix.
  • Integer division by zero (traps on x86, not on ARM): build with -fsanitize=integer-divide-by-zero -fno-sanitize-recover=all added to CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS, CXX17FLAGS and LDFLAGS. Use R_MAKEVARS_USER=<file> R CMD INSTALL --library=<tmp lib>, then run the examples (tools::Rd2ex per Rd file) against it. Raylib uses R’s flags, so it’s covered too.
  • gcc/LTO warnings: Docker works here. R-hub’s containers (e.g. ghcr.io/r-hub/containers/gcc-asan:latest, --platform linux/amd64) can compile and link single files with their R flags. Some warnings only appear at the LTO link step.
  • webR demos: headless Chrome via puppeteer-core in a temp folder, using /Applications/Google Chrome.app. Capture pageerror and console output, and take screenshots. A SharedArrayBuffer is not defined error on the first load is normal: the service worker reloads the page with the right headers.
  • Missing webR symbols: list the function imports of raylibr/libs/raylibr.so from the deployed package with Node (WebAssembly.Module.imports). No raylibr function should be imported. “resolved is not a function” in the browser means a missing symbol.

3.3 Releasing

  1. Bump Version in DESCRIPTION, and turn “development version” in NEWS.md into the version.
  2. Local CRAN check, plus checkbashisms configure cleanup (installed with Homebrew).
  3. Push, then wait for CI (check, codegen, pkgdown, webR) and R-hub: gh workflow run rhub.yaml --ref main -f config="linux,macos-arm64,windows,gcc16,clang23,clang-ubsan,gcc-asan,lto,nosuggests". The dispatch sometimes returns HTTP 500; retry after 30 s.
  4. git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "raylibr X.Y.Z" <commit>, push the tag, then gh release create vX.Y.Z --notes-file <NEWS section> --verify-tag.
  5. win-builder: FTP is blocked here, so devtools::check_win_devel() fails. Upload through the HTTPS form at https://win-builder.r-project.org/upload.aspx with curl: GET the page for __VIEWSTATE, __VIEWSTATEGENERATOR and __EVENTVALIDATION, then POST multipart with FileUpload2/Button2 (R-devel) or FileUpload1/Button1 (R-release). Success shows the uploaded file’s name and size. “Access to the path … is denied” means it’s already queued.
  6. Update cran-comments.md and submit (maintainer).

3.4 CI notes

  • check.yaml: Windows installs Mesa llvmpipe into R’s bin, and Linux uses Xvfb; both set RAYLIBR_GL=true. macOS skips window tests.
  • pkgdown.yaml and webr.yaml both push to gh-pages, and retry once after 30 s if their pushes collide. pages.yaml (added by the maintainer) publishes gh-pages.
  • codegen.yaml pins roxygen2 7.3.3 and installs the X11/GL headers.
  • rhub.yaml installs the X11/GL headers in its Linux jobs (step added by hand to the generated file).
  • git push and the GitHub API occasionally fail for a moment here; retry.
